# `Q-20-8` — Multiple Formats Declared, Only One Rendered

> The document's `format:` declares more than one output format, but
> Quarto renders only one per invocation.

## What this means

A document's front matter declared more than one key under `format:`
(for example `format: {docx: default, html: default}`), but a single
`q2 render` invocation produces exactly one output. Quarto picked one
of the declared formats to render — either the one named by an
explicit `--to`, or the first key declared — and the rest were
skipped entirely. This warning names which format was used and which
were skipped, so the skipped ones don't go missing silently.

## Why this happens

- A document was ported from a workflow (or from Quarto 1 project
  configuration) where multiple formats render in a single pass, and
  the `format:` block was carried over unchanged.
- A document intentionally declares more than one format as a menu of
  options, expecting the caller to pick one with `--to` on each
  invocation — which is the supported pattern, but it produces this
  warning on every invocation that doesn't use `--to`.

## How to fix

- If you only ever want one of the declared formats, remove the
  others from `format:` and keep a single scalar or single-key map.
- If you want multiple formats from the same source, render once per
  format with an explicit `--to`, e.g. `q2 render doc.qmd --to docx`
  and `q2 render doc.qmd --to html` as two separate invocations.
